clue.text: Attractive part of the world?

parts.note: read 'attractive' as 'that attracts': the place on Earth toward which a compass needle is pulled

explanation.definitionFit: This is the point near the pole that a compass needle points to, pulled there by the planet's magnetism.

clue.text: Mutilates the old-fashioned linen presses

definitions.meaning: old household machines that squeezed water out of washing between rollers

explanation.surface: Someone damages the antique laundry machines.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to damage badly; the noun was a wringer with rollers for wet laundry.

clue.text: Figs are chopped up, giving warmth

indicators.note: chopping something up breaks it into bits, so these letters are cut and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Diced figs somehow provide heat, like a kitchen paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' sounds like cookery, but it tells you to rearrange FIGS and ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A household heater burning mains fuel is what gives a room warmth; the definition describes the appliance's function.

clue.text: Badly maims Eastern leaders

indicators.note: doing something badly garbles it, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Some cruel person wounds rulers from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Muslim prayer leaders or religious heads, figures of the East in the setter's sense.

clue.text: Claws common little boys

definitions.meaning: an informal word for small children, especially lads

explanation.surface: Grabbing hands belong to ordinary young lads.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab pincers are one sense; a colloquial British term for small kids is the other.

clue.text: Drops innumerable quantities of them doing this

definitions.text: Drops innumerable quantities of them doing this

parts.words: Drops innumerable quantities of them doing this
parts.note: countless drops of water falling from the sky describe wet weather in progress

explanation.definitionFit: Countless water droplets coming down from clouds is what wet weather consists of.

clue.text: He gets the lot!

parts.note: 'the lot' looks like 'everything' but is an item for sale at an auction

explanation.definitionFit: At auction the person offering most wins the item, called a lot.

clue.text: Called to say two are going to join up

definitions.text: Called to say two are going to join up

parts.words: Called to say two are going to join up
parts.note: a church announcement, read out ahead of a wedding, that a couple intend to marry

explanation.definitionFit: These are proclamations made in church that a couple plan to wed; they are said to be 'called'.

clue.text: They keep us covered in water…

definitions.text: They keep us covered in water…

parts.words: They keep us covered in water
parts.note: items that preserve a swimmer's modesty while in the sea or pool

explanation.definitionFit: Shorts worn for swimming keep a man decent while he is in the water.

clue.text: Pushing down hard, a foot at a time

definitions.text: Pushing down hard, a foot at a time

parts.words: Pushing down hard, a foot at a time
parts.note: crushing something underfoot by stamping step after step

explanation.definitionFit: Treading heavily on something, step by step, crushes it underfoot.

clue.text: And it's for pulling water beneath it

definitions.text: And it's for pulling water beneath it

parts.words: And it's for pulling water beneath it
parts.note: a small vessel that sits on water and hauls larger ships

explanation.definitionFit: A harbour vessel tows bigger ships while floating on the sea.

clue.text: Counting and recounting

definitions.meaning: reckoning a number, as tellers count votes or cash

explanation.walkthrough: 'recounting' looks like counting a second time, but here it means narrating.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both totting up (as a bank teller does) and narrating a tale.

clue.text: From Lord Lister, I learn how the operating theatre should be

definitions.text: how the operating theatre should be

indicators.note: 'from' says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A medical student takes a lesson on surgical hygiene from Joseph Lister.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister was the Victorian surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgery room must be free of germs, which is the clinical sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Child is to try and get damages

parts.note: taken as written
to sue is to take legal action for compensation

explanation.surface: A kid is going to court seeking compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring, especially in legal language, as in 'died without'.

clue.text: A failure to notice it's above sense

parts.note: over means above
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Missing something is said to be beyond mere perception.
explanation.definitionFit: An unintentional omission, something missed through not looking properly.

clue.text: Reached a roundabout without five hundred getting hurt in the head

indicators.note: roundabout suggests going round in circles, so the letters are muddled
without means the following letter is left out of the word before

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone drove round a traffic island minus a Roman numeral and got hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without five hundred' drops D from REACHED, leaving REACHE; with A that gives REACHEA, which 'roundabout' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the ear is a hurt inside the head.

clue.text: Recover, and become more skilful

explanation.surface: Getting over an illness and also improving one's game.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both recuperating and improving one's ability.

clue.text: Is drawn back from fire? No, to it

definitions.text: Is drawn back from fire? No, to it

parts.words: Is drawn back from fire? No, to it
parts.note: a part of a gun that is pulled back in order to shoot, not retreating from flames

explanation.definitionFit: The lever a shooter pulls back to discharge a gun.

clue.text: It's written down for "Pie, lest changes occur

indicators.note: when changes occur, the letters given are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A note on paper warns that a pie may be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter, as in the New Testament books, is a written composition.

clue.text: Fabulous bird goes back to foreign soldier to get a dog

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of legend
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A mythical bird retreats to a soldier from abroad to get a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged Welsh breed, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Study is over-so overlook it

parts.note: to con is to study carefully
done means finished, over

explanation.surface: Study is finished, so let it pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to forgive or turn a blind eye to wrongdoing.

clue.text: Spanish river, to us, is very wild

parts.note: rio is Spanish for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river in Spain seems untamed to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly, disorderly, wildly uncontrolled.

clue.text: Quite spoiling someone? Certainly not by over-indulgence!

definitions.text: Quite spoiling someone? Certainly not by over-indulgence!

parts.words: Quite spoiling someone? Certainly not by over-indulgence!
parts.note: spoiling in the sense of wrecking utterly, not pampering a child

explanation.definitionFit: Wrecking completely is the destructive sense of spoiling, not the pampering one.

clue.text: Food in the wood

definitions.meaning: cereal crops such as wheat and oats
the pattern of fibres in timber

explanation.surface: Something to eat found in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal seed is food; the lie of fibres in timber has the same name.

clue.text: High flyer's pointless agreement

indicators.note: without a point: a compass point letter is removed

parts.note: the supersonic airliner Concorde flew very high

explanation.surface: An airline pilot's agreement is said to be meaningless.
explanation.walkthrough: E (east) is a compass point, so 'pointless' takes it from CONCORDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony or accord between parties.

clue.text: I.e., agent to change and parley

indicators.note: change here means the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: That is, a spy must switch sides and hold talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is part of the fodder, not a link: IEAGENTTO rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To parley is to hold talks and bargain.

clue.text: Love grim Northern scent

parts.note: O is zero, love in tennis
dour, a word of Scottish origin, means grim

explanation.surface: A grim northerner's love has an aroma.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell, whether pleasant or not.

clue.text: Ship emergent S.A.S. out to military quarters

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the Special Air Service regiment
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship sends the special forces out to their barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: SS from 'Ship' goes at the end, after the anagram of EMERGENT and SAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The dining room and club for non-commissioned officers in a barracks.
